meanings.note: Больной ребёнок = a sick child. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sick, ill; (as a noun) patient').
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sick, ill; (as a noun) patient').
colloquial insult: ты больной? = are you crazy?

examples.trans: I have a sick child.
Are you crazy or what?

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
I don't need any more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Male sibling. Common masculine noun meaning 'brother, cousin' in everyday Russian.
in двоюродный/троюродный брат, often shortened to брат

examples.trans: And this is cousin Vsevolod.

examples.text: Мой старший брат живёт в Москве.
examples.trans: My older brother lives in Moscow.

examples.text: А это брат Всеволод. Мы очень переживаем.
examples.trans: And this is cousin Vsevolod. We're very worried.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?
Suddenly it began to rain.

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!
You're my friend, after all.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('видеорегистратор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'on the dashcam' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всё чётко записано на моём видеорегистраторе.
examples.trans: Everything is clearly recorded on my dashcam.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть видеорегистратор.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always on the dashcam.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, that is all.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it.
Don't talk nonsense.

examples.text: Да ерунда, мне даже нравится. Как тебе твой новый кандидат?
examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it. How do you like your new candidate?

заодно.gloss: at the same time, while I'm at it

meanings.en: at the same time, while one is at it
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'одно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'одно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: And at the same time I'll trim the branches in the yard.
Buy bread and milk while you're at it.

examples.text: Заодно без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: At the same time without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писанный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('recorded').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень записанный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very recorded choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто записанный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply recorded day at the restaurant today.

записать.gloss: to write down; to save (a contact)

meanings.note: Записан как... = saved as. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write down; to save (a contact)', paired with 'записывать'.

Записан как... = saved as. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write down; to save (a contact)', paired with 'записывать'.

examples.text: Я знаю, как я у тебя записан.
examples.trans: I know what I'm saved as in your phone.
Write down my number.

examples.text: Я знаю, как я у тебя в телефоне записан. Свин.
examples.trans: I know what I'm saved as in your phone. 'Pig'.

meanings.note: Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

examples.trans: So you're not coming?
So that's it.
Then make sure he does.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her

examples.trans: Mum, where's my phone?
My mum is a doctor.
Mum, what's a bidet?

meanings.note: + genitive plural: много дел. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Comparative. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Too much to do.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
That's mine.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: молодой человек = young man (polite address)

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?
They have a young family.

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'давно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We recently returned from Paris.
I still work as a cook.
Moreover, that was quite recently.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'замужний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('unmarried').

examples.text: У мамы вдруг появляется молодая незамужняя подруга.
examples.trans: Mom suddenly has a young unmarried friend.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень незамужний выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very unmarried choice.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'чего').

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.
I have nothing to lose.
There is nothing to do here.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

обижаться.gloss: to take offence, to be hurt

meanings.en: to take offence, to get upset
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take offence, to be hurt', paired with 'обидеться'.

examples.trans: Don't take offence, Vanya.
Don't be offended by my words.

examples.text: Да не обижайся ты, Ваня. Сейчас найду подходящую одежду.
examples.trans: Don't take offence, Vanya. I'll find suitable clothes right now.

meanings.note: Firm promise or requirement. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.
I will definitely come tomorrow.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: From that place. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'туда').
Away from that location. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'туда').

examples.text: Я же тебе говорил: пошли оттуда!
examples.trans: I told you: let us leave that place!

examples.text: Надо было силой меня оттуда уводить!
examples.trans: You should have dragged me away from there by force!

переехать.gloss: to move (to a new home or city)

meanings.note: Переехать в Москву. Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to move (to a new home or city)', paired with 'переезжать'.

examples.trans: You moved to Moscow, right?
They moved into a new flat.

examples.text: Ты в Москву переехала, да? Поедем сейчас в сауну, посидим!
examples.trans: You moved to Moscow, right? Let's go to a sauna now and sit for a while!

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Talk to him.
We need to talk.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'руга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'female friend, girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll invite a female friend over.
She is my best friend.

examples.text: Пять тысяч рублей. Я подругу приглашу.
examples.trans: Five thousand roubles. I'll invite a female friend over.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Used in the singular. Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.trans: Call the police!
The police are here.

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I understand.
I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'являться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to appear'.

examples.text: Нам не надо появляться на работе вместе.
examples.trans: We do not need to appear at work together.

examples.text: Нам лучше пока не появляться на работе вместе по утрам.
examples.trans: We had better not show up at work together in the mornings for now.

examples.text: В меню каждую весну появляются новые лёгкие салаты.
examples.trans: New light salads appear on the menu every spring.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Не расстраивайся = don't be upset. Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'страиваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get upset, to worry', paired with 'расстроиться'.

examples.trans: The car is insured, don't be upset.
And the car is insured, don't be upset.
Alright, come on, don't be upset.

meanings.en: dear, darling, my friend (in address: родной мой)
meanings.note: Often used ironically. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('native, own; dear, darling').
родной брат = full brother; родной город = hometown

examples.text: Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: Well then, my dear friend, to you!
This is my hometown.

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give me your hand.
I shake your hand! (a goodbye)
Right, cheers then.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: colloquial: нет света = the power is off
colloquial: нет света = the power is off
В целом свете = in the whole world. Common masculine noun meaning 'light; electricity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Turn on the light.
Three districts without electricity.

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

сводить.gloss: to bring together (концы с концами сводить = make ends meet)

meanings.note: in idiom сводить концы с концами = make ends meet

examples.trans: I can barely make ends meet.

examples.text: На такую зарплату трудно сводить концы с концами.
examples.trans: It is hard to make ends meet on such a salary.

examples.text: Я двенадцать тысяч получаю! Еле концы с концами свожу.
examples.trans: I get twelve thousand! I can barely make ends meet.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Perfective of мочь. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be able, to manage', paired with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.

meanings.note: Intentionally. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пециально'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

Терять время. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.trans: You're wasting your time.

examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: You're fired!
He was fired.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

уехать.gloss: to leave, to go away (by vehicle)

meanings.note: By car, train etc. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (by vehicle)', paired with 'уезжать'.

examples.trans: I'll be gone for an hour.
He has gone to Moscow.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Хватит!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: There wasn't enough money.
That's enough!

examples.text: Лёва, отвечай шефу быстро и чётко!
